title: MetaICL: Learning to Learn In Context
abstract: Sewon Min, Mike Lewis, Luke Zettlemoyer, Hannaneh Hajishirzi. Proceedings of the 2022 Conference of the North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies. 2022.

claims.text: MetaICL tunes a pretrained language model on a large collection of meta-training tasks using an in-context learning objective to improve few-shot performance on unseen target tasks without parameter updates at test time.
Channel MetaICL consistently outperforms standard MetaICL, multi-task zero-shot transfer, and raw language model in-context learning baselines across multiple task evaluation splits.
Performance gains of MetaICL over multi-task zero-shot baselines are particularly significant when target tasks involve domain or task format shifts relative to meta-training tasks.
Meta-training on a diverse set of task formats and capabilities yields higher target task performance compared to meta-training on a non-diverse task set.
MetaICL applied to GPT-2 Large (770M parameters) matches or outperforms raw language model in-context learning using GPT-J (6B parameters).
MetaICL and human-written instructions are complementary, with the best performance achieved by combining both methods.
Multi-task zero-shot transfer without in-context training does not outperform raw language model in-context baselines when using a 770M parameter model.

limitations.text: In-context learning approaches require longer sequence contexts during training and inference due to concatenating multiple training examples, making inference less computationally efficient than zero-shot baselines.
Experiments are evaluated primarily on classification and multiple-choice tasks with predefined candidate label sets rather than free-form text generation.
When semantic information in label words is removed by replacing labels with random English words, overall MetaICL task performance drops significantly.
Standard in-context learning on raw language models suffers from high output variance and sensitivity to prompt ordering or template engineering.
Multi-task zero-shot learning methods rely heavily on human-written task templates that require significant manual prompt engineering.

future_work.text: Extend MetaICL meta-training to masked language models and larger parameter scale models.
Apply MetaICL to broader NLP task formats including free-form text generation.
Develop systematic selection frameworks to identify which meta-training tasks are most helpful for specific downstream target tasks.
Improve in-context meta-learning methods to outperform meta-trained fully supervised fine-tuned models.

methodologies.name: MetaICL (Meta-training for In-Context Learning)
methodologies.description: Tunes a language model by sampling k+1 training examples from a meta-training task, conditioning on the first k examples, and training the model using cross-entropy loss to predict the output of the (k+1)-th example.

methodologies.name: Channel MetaICL
methodologies.description: A noisy channel variant of MetaICL that flips input and label pairs in the prompt sequence to model conditional probabilities P(x|y).
